## Data Quality

- 239 videos with zero duration (24,076 train rows affected)
- 15,609 exact duplicate rows in the training-period log
- Sentinel: is_live_streamer = -124 on 21,127 of 27,285 user rows
- UNKNOWN values: user_active_degree (6), video_type (1), upload_type (80)
- Constant columns: is_lowactive_period, visible_status, is_rand
- hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8
- The training-period log begins on 20220409, not 20220408

## Feature Coverage

- Video features: 100.000 % of train+valid video IDs found in the feature table
- User features: 100.000 % of train+valid user IDs found in the profile table

## Leakage Flag

The video statistics table is a period aggregate over full-platform traffic.
Implied total shows: 12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged
exposures (ratio approximately 4,892 to one). Observation periods per video
range 45 to 181, exceeding the interaction log span.
Legal for use, but any feature derived from it must be caveated as leaky.

## Metric Conventions

- Task: within-user ranking (each user's impressions ranked against each other)
- nDCG@5: sorts by score with a stable sort (ties fall back to row order)
- AUC: averages ranks over ties (Mann-Whitney U)
- GAUC: per-user AUC, only users with 0 < positives < impressions,
  weighted by positive count
- Zero-positive users: nDCG recorded as 0.0 and included in the average
- Primary score = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5)

## Measured Dead Ends

- Adding all 13 static feature fields: primary 0.5940 vs 0.5950 for the default 5
- Embedding dimension k = 8 / 16 / 32: primary 0.5895 / 0.5902 / 0.5887 (flat)
- The bottleneck is not features or capacity
- First-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0 to within-user ranking
  (any term constant within a user does not change intra-group ordering)


ROLE: EDA Builder

Return concise JSON: at most 3 findings, 3 feature candidates, and 3 UI notes. One sentence per field.

feature_candidates.description: One-hot encode the tab field (0-14) as input features for the ranking model.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures tab-specific long_view propensity, directly usable in bpr/group_softmax scoring.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add tab_id integer to feature mapping; transform to one-hot in model input (dimension 15).
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None; tab is observed at serving time and in train/valid.
feature_candidates.name: tab_one_hot

feature_candidates.description: Compute prior-day or prior-window long_view rate per video from train history, excluding the current session period.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Adds recency-weighted popularity signal that is not leaky and may improve ranking for trending items.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Build chronological aggregates per video from train; use only data strictly before each impression's timestamp.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Safe only if computed without future information; must avoid using the full-period video statistics table.
feature_candidates.name: lagged_video_popularity

feature_candidates.description: Aggregate per-user historical long_view count and click rate within the same tab from prior interactions.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: User+tab interaction history captures contextual engagement intensity beyond global user or video stats.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Maintain rolling counts by (user, tab) using only past interactions; add as side features to model.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Safe if computed strictly from past rows; ensure no future user actions are used.
feature_candidates.name: user_tab_history

findings.implication: Tab identity is a strong within-user discriminator; one-hot tab features or tab-specific user history should boost GAUC/nDCG.
findings.observation: Tab-wise train long_view rates range from tab 4 at 48.93% to tab 0 at 4.22%, with tab 1 at 38.61%.
findings.title: Tab long_view rate varies widely

findings.implication: Direct use of these aggregates would leak future information; only lagged versions computed from prior periods are valid.
findings.observation: The video statistics table is a platform aggregate over ~4,892x the logged traffic, with observation periods longer than the log span.
findings.title: Video statistics are full-period leaky

findings.implication: Duplicates and zero-duration rows must be removed or capped before computing user-history or video-popularity aggregates to avoid bias.
findings.observation: Train log contains 15,609 exact duplicate rows and 239 zero-duration videos affecting 24,076 rows.
findings.title: Data quality issues distort aggregates

data.recommended_next_focus: Implement tab one-hot and user-tab historical long_view aggregates, evaluate on validation GAUC/nDCG; if gain, experiment with lagged video popularity.
data.summary: EDA from the data card shows strong tab-based long_view rate spread (tab 4 48.9% vs tab 0 4.2%), confirming tab context as a promising within-user signal. The video statistics table is flagged as leaky (full-period aggregate), so only lagged variants are safe. Duplicate rows and zero-duration videos require cleaning before historical aggregates.
